To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the incorporation of PMDA and PPD into ODPA-MDA polyimide can enhance the Tg of the final polyimides without sacrificing the thermo-oxidative properties and processing properties.
the introduction of PMDA and PPD into the backbone of ODPA-MDA PMR-type polyamic acid could significantly improve the thermo-oxidative properties and mechanical properties of polyimides.

the incorporation of PMDA into OM increased the crosslink density and enhanced the thermo-oxidative resistance of OPM, while the incorporation of PPD into OM increased the Tg of OMP without sacrificing the thermal properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new PMR-type polymeric materials for advanced composites.
the synthesis and characterisation of a novel PMR polyimide based OMPM, OPM and OMP, and a comparison of the thermal properties of the three systems.
the development of a new class of PMR polyimides with improved thermal and mechanical properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the incorporation of PMDA and PPD could increase Tg of the polyimide by 50°C, while retaining comparable thermal stability, reasonable processing properties and mechanical properties.
the thermal properties were mainly determined by the crosslink density, while the processing and mechanical properties were influenced by the crosslink and the chemical structure of the backbone.

the incorporation of a second dianhydrides and diamine into the backbone of ODPA-MDA PMR-type polyimidic oligomers can enhance the thermal properties of polyimides, and the endcap groups can also influence the thermal properties of these oligomers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the incorporation of PPD or PMDA into the OM backbone could improve the thermo-oxidative properties, but the improvement was more significant for the OPM than the OMP.
OPM, which contained a high amount of PMDA in the backbone, showed the best overall properties, while OMP was the most thermally stable.

the introduction of PMDA or PMDA-PPD copolymerisation to ODPA-MDA could improve the Tg, without significantly sacrificing thermo-oxidative and processing properties, which would make these novel PMR polyimides more promising in aerospace applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the thermal properties of the polyimide are not only determined by the chemical structure but also by the crosslink density.

the crosslink density is the most important factor for improving the thermo-oxidative properties of PMR polyimides, and the crosslinking efficiency is determined by the chemical structure of the backbone and the endcaps.
the thermal properties of the PMR-type polyimidised oligomers are strongly dependent upon the chemical structure of the backbone and the endcaps.
